claims.statement: Stonehenge developed over many generations. The first earthwork was built around 3000 BCE; the main stone settings followed around 2500 BCE. The early monument was also a burial place. Later changes included rearranging the bluestones and creating the Avenue towards the River Avon.

claims.statement: The map marks the archaeological site, using the Heritage Gateway reference coordinates.
Around 3000 BCE, people built a circular ditch and banks at Stonehenge. Cremated remains were buried within and around the monument.

claims.statement: The map marks the archaeological site, using the Heritage Gateway reference coordinates.
Around 2500 BCE, builders erected the large sarsens and smaller bluestones at the centre of Stonehenge.

value.text: Around 2500 BCE, builders erected the large sarsens and smaller bluestones at the centre of Stonehenge.

claims.statement: The map marks the archaeological site, using the Heritage Gateway reference coordinates.
Bluestones were rearranged and the Avenue was built around 2300–2200 BCE. The Y and Z pits date to around 1800–1500 BCE. These were separate episodes, not continuous building work.
